what_it_is: An open-source Python library and a set of datasets for data-driven engineering design optimisation, aimed at machine-learning methods such as inverse design with generative models and surrogate-based optimisation, not at language models (pp. 1-3). It wraps seven simulation-backed design problems (airfoil shape optimisation with RANS CFD, 2D and 3D heat-conduction topology optimisation, thermoelastic and structural beam topology optimisation, a photonic demultiplexer, a DC-DC power converter) behind one API, with datasets, constraint checks and adjoint optimisers (pp. 5-8). A companion library, EngiOpt, provides baselines (GANs, conditional GANs, diffusion models, MLP+NSGA-II), compared on cumulative optimality gap, constraint violations, MMD and DPP diversity over 10 seeds (pp. 3-4, 8-9).
domain: engineering design optimisation for machine learning: aerodynamics, heat transfer, structural topology, photonics, power electronics (pp. 6-8)
size: 7 problems with datasets (Table 1, p. 7); the baselines are ML models, and no LLM is evaluated (p. 8)
source_of_items: simulation datasets generated with the library's simulators, several replicating set-ups from earlier publications (pp. 5-6)

evaluation: ML design metrics: cumulative optimality gap, ratio of violated constraints, ratio of failed simulations, MMD and DPP diversity (pp. 3-4)
human_validation: none reported; the problem implementations are described as rigorously tested and versioned (pp. 2, 6)

facts_to_cite: EngiBench (Felten et al.) is an open-source library and set of datasets for data-driven engineering design (p. 1).
It targets inverse design and surrogate modelling with machine-learning models, not language models (pp. 2-3, 8).
It implements seven simulation-backed design problems (p. 7).
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares only an engineering setting and the use of physics simulators. It has no language-model evaluation, no reasoning task, no gold traces and no step-level evaluation; its benchmark compares ML optimisers and generative models on design datasets (pp. 7-9).
